source_title: nathanliow/atlas-of-physics: An interactive 3D textbook for AP Physics 1 and AP Physics C - GitHub
source_excerpt:
An interactive textbook. Each chapter is one simple motion drawn in 3D like a textbook diagram (paper solids, ink edges, one lit thing). No apparatus: only the moving object, its vectors, axes and graphs. Scroll turns the pages and moves the camera; hover lights a thing; click breaks it down (a vector into components, a graph into slope and area).
Tools need npm install (puppeteer-core) and Chrome (set CHROME to its path if not at the macOS default). Screenshots: CHAPTER=newton PARTS=rest:0,car:5 node tools/shoot.mjs shots/newton (PARTS = key or key:page)
Run: python3 -m http.server 8137 (any static server; three.js loads from jsDelivr) and open http://127.0.0.1:8137/ Keys: ← → turn pages, Esc puts a part back. Links: newton/#4 opens page 2.4. Phones and tablets: the figure stacks over the text, swipes snap to whole pages, a tap breaks a part down; resolution steps down by itself if frames run slow.
AP® is a trademark of the College Board, which does not endorse this site. The equation sheet follows the published AP Physics equation tables.
